messages:
anya: Heads-up: on very narrow phones the Monitoring table compresses and you cant reach the right-side actions without horizontal scroll. Worse: our left-edge swipe to open the nav conflicts with attempting to pan the table. Screenshot in thread.

dante: ah yeah. which container handles the scroll? is it a native overflow or a JS virtualized list?

anya: native overflow on .monitoring-list, rows are fixed-height but with lots of columns (status, model, duration, region, tags, actions). We rely on overflow-x: auto.

ting: two quick paths: 1) reduce columns on small widths (hide tags+region), collapse actions into a single menu; 2) change interactions: stack rows as cards at <=360px so no horizontal scroll.

anya: also noticed focus issues: when keyboard navigation reaches the leftmost cell it sometimes moves focus to the global nav. Might be because the nav has tabindex=0 for accessibility.

dante: simple interim CSS: add touch-action: pan-x to the inner scroller so it prefers horizontal pans. Also raise the edge-swipe activation distance so we don't trigger nav unless swipe starts very near edge and is >30px.

ting: good. For final UX I prefer stacked cards for density parity with other mobile screens (See mock). But stacked cards increase vertical scrolling. Maybe we do a progressive collapse: at <=380px switch to compact rows with two-line summary, at <=340px use stacked cards.

anya: love the progressive thresholds. copy/accessibility notes: truncate long model names with aria-label for full name, ensure action menu buttons have aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. Also ensure the action menu is reachable via keyboard without invoking nav.

dante: implement quick fix now: touch-action + increase swipe threshold. Ting can prototype progressive collapse in Figma. I'll open a tiny PR for the touch-action hotfix.

prod-bot: deploy-preview created: https://deployments.redwood/preview/1843216789  includes touch-action change, increased swipe threshold and truncated-name aria updates. Build OK.

anya: tested on Android small devices and iPhone 8 emulator. touch-action helps a lot; edge swipe still catches super aggressive flicks on iOS. Stacked card mock looks fine but need to validate metrics (how many rows per screen).

ting: will run a small usability pass and add hit-target guidance (44px min). Also reword header from "Monitoring" to "Live requests" per product lexicon.

dante: plan: ship touch-action fix today, iterate stacked-card breakpoints next sprint, add A/B to 10% traffic to compare accidental nav opens and action success rate. Good to go? :thumbsup:

anya: yes. PR link when ready and I'll attach the Figma frames.
